name: Headings
summary: Use semantic heading elements and GOV.UK heading classes to create a consistent, navigable content hierarchy.
rules: Use h1 through h6 elements for document structure and apply govuk-heading-xl, -l, -m or -s for visual size.
Ordinarily use one clear h1, then descend through heading levels without choosing elements for their appearance.
For common question pages, pair h1 with govuk-heading-l, h2 with govuk-heading-m and lower headings with the next suitable size.
Use heading captions to provide context above a heading without replacing the heading itself.
accessibility: A heading level must reflect nesting in the page outline even when its GOV.UK size class differs.
Do not use bold paragraphs as visual headings because screen-reader heading navigation will miss them.
Any deliberate visual and semantic hierarchy mismatch needs accessibility testing in its full context.
restrictions: Do not select a heading element solely to obtain its default browser size or margin.
Avoid very long headings; simplify the content and keep the page purpose clear.
